{{short description|Canadian mathematician}}
'''Monica A. Nevins''' (born 1973){{r|born}} is a Canadian mathematician, and a professor of mathematics and statistics at the [[University of Ottawa]]. Her research interests include [[abstract algebra]], [[representation theory]], [[algebraic group]]s, and mathematical [[cryptography]].

==Education and career==
Nevins went to high school in [[Val-d'Or]], Quebec. She graduated from the [[University of Ottawa]] in 1994, and completed a PhD in mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1998.{{r|bio}} Her dissertation, ''Admissible Nilpotent Coadjoint Orbits of p-adic Reductive Lie Groups'', was supervised by [[David Vogan]].{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research at the [[University of Alberta]], Nevins joined the faculty of the University of Ottawa, where she was promoted to full professor in 2014.{{r|bio}}

==Recognition==
Nevins was the 2010–2011 winner of the University of Ottawa Award for Excellence in Teaching.{{r|xl}}
She was elected as a fellow of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] in 2019.{{r|cmsf}}

==Personal==
Monica married Ralph Nevins, who is a computer scientist and mathematical artist.{{r|ralph}}
